inline_comments.comment: Commented-out debug `logger.info` call should be removed before merging. Per project guidelines, `console.log` and equivalent diagnostic calls must not be committed; inspect intermediate values through assertions or proper logging instead.

`getChangedFiles()` already calls `getRepoRoot()` internally, and `getRepoRoot()` is also called directly in the same `Promise.all`. Because both start concurrently, the `this.repoRoot` cache is unset when both begin, causing two `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` subprocesses to be spawned. Simplify by awaiting `getRepoRoot()` first and passing it to `getChangedFiles()`, or restructure `getChangedFiles()` to return `{ repoRoot, changes }` so the root is fetched exactly once.

`changedFile.replace(\`${repoRoot}/\`, '')` strips the repo root prefix using a hardcoded `/` separator. On Windows, `resolve()` produces paths with `\` separators, so the template literal `\`${repoRoot}/\`` never matches and the full absolute path is stored as the "changed file" label instead of the relative one. Use `path.relative` which is path-separator-aware:
```ts
changedStoryFiles.add(path.relative(repoRoot, changedFile));
```
`path` is already imported at the top of the file via `import { resolve } from 'node:path'` — add `relative` to the import.

`ChangeDetectionService` is exported here without any stability prefix, while the companion `getChangeDetectionReadiness` exported two lines above is aliased to `experimental_getChangeDetectionReadiness`. The inconsistency signals different stability guarantees that probably aren't intentional. If this API is still experimental, export it as `experimental_ChangeDetectionService`; if it's intended to be stable, that should be a deliberate decision and documented.

`ChangeDetectionService` is exported twice from this file: once implicitly through `export { … } from './change-detection'` (since `change-detection/index.ts` already re-exports it from `./service`), and again explicitly here from `'./change-detection/service'`. The direct path export is redundant — remove it and rely solely on the barrel export.

`vi.clearAllMocks()` is called in both `beforeEach` and `afterEach`. The `afterEach` call is redundant — `beforeEach` already ensures a clean state before each test. Remove the `afterEach` block (or consolidate) to avoid confusion about which hook is authoritative.

`internal_resetChangeDetectionReadiness()` is called in both `beforeEach` (line ~63) and `afterEach` (line ~67). The `afterEach` call is redundant since `beforeEach` unconditionally resets state before each test. Remove the duplicate from `afterEach` to keep reset logic in one canonical place.

general_comments.comment: `git-diff-provider.ts` imports `execa` from `'execa'` for use in production code, but `execa` is listed only in `devDependencies` of `code/core/package.json`. When `@storybook/core` is installed as a dependency in a consumer project, `execa` will not be present and the runtime import will fail. Additionally, both `git-diff-provider.ts` and its test carry `// eslint-disable-next-line depend/ban-dependencies` — the `depend/ban-dependencies` ESLint rule is a deliberate guard against importing banned packages. Suppressing it without explanation signals that either (a) `execa` should be moved to `dependencies` (and added to the allowlist), or (b) the git operations should be rewritten using Node's built-in `child_process.execFile` / `spawnSync` to avoid the banned dependency entirely.

`CHANGE_DETECTION_STATUS_TYPE_ID` is exported from `change-detection/index.ts` but is not re-exported from `core-server/index.ts`, even though `ChangeDetectionService` (which depends on it) is exported there. Any external consumer of `ChangeDetectionService` who needs to look up statuses by type ID would have to reach into an internal module path. Either export it alongside the service (e.g. `export { CHANGE_DETECTION_STATUS_TYPE_ID } from './change-detection'`) or document why it is intentionally withheld.
